passage:
At nine at night, with a viva the next morning, Arnab's phone lit up with a message from a batchmate: "Is it true you're quitting engineering? Sorry to hear that." The only person he had told was Kalyani. His face went hot.

He wanted to type something cruel. He even opened the note where he kept what Kalyani had once confided about her failed paper, then closed it. Instead he wrote to her: "Can we talk after the viva? Just us."

The next day, on the library steps, he said, "I told only you. Now half the class knows. I'm angry, and I want to know what happened." Kalyani stared at her shoes. "I told one person. I didn't think it would go anywhere." Arnab nodded slowly. He didn't hug her. From now on he would share smaller things and watch what came back.

qa.q: What was Arnab feeling when he read the message, and what did he nearly do?
qa.a: Angry and exposed, with his face hot. He nearly used Kalyani's own confided secret against her but closed the note.

qa.q: What did Arnab do wisely in this situation?
qa.a: He waited until after the viva, asked to talk privately, told Kalyani how he felt and did not leak her secret in return.

qa.q: How might Kalyani have felt on the library steps?
qa.a: Ashamed or defensive. She stared at her shoes and said she didn't think it would go anywhere.

grounding: Arnab's secret spreads; he feels exposed and furious, confronts Kalyani privately and decides how much to trust her.
